title: Order Book: Best Bid, Best Ask, Spread

statement.md: An exchange's limit order book collects resting orders to buy (bids) and to sell (asks). The two numbers every market participant watches are the best bid (highest price anyone will pay) and the best ask (lowest price anyone will accept); their difference, the spread, is the instantaneous cost of crossing the market. You will maintain a simplified book under a stream of events and print the top of book after every event.

rows: Add qty shares resting at the given price on the given side.
Cancel: remove qty shares resting at that price on that side.

statement.md: side is B for the bid side or S for the ask side. price is an integer number of cents (1005 means 10.05). Quantities at the same price accumulate: two adds of 10 at the same bid price leave 20 resting there. A cancel reduces the resting quantity at that price; when it reaches exactly 0 the price level disappears from the book. Events arrive and take effect one at a time.

After each event, print the top of book: the best bid, the best ask, and the spread (best ask minus best bid). Each of the three fields is printed as dollars with exactly 2 decimal places (integer cents divided by 100, e.g. 1005 -> 10.05). If a side has no resting orders print a single dash - in its place; the spread is printed only when both sides are present, otherwise it is also -.

statement.title: Reading the top of book
statement.md: Level-1 data (best bid/ask/size) is the most consumed market data feed in existence: every spread capture, quote-span statistic, and markout calculation starts from it. Note that this book never crosses: the best bid never exceeds the best ask in any test, so the spread is always >= 0.00 when both sides exist.

inputFormat: Line 1: the integer n (number of events). Each of the next n lines contains four whitespace-separated tokens: T side price qty where T is A or C, side is B or S, price is an integer number of cents (1 <= price <= 10^6), and qty is a positive integer (1 <= qty <= 10^6).
outputFormat: Print n lines, one per event, in order. Each line has three space-separated fields: BEST_BID BEST_ASK SPREAD. Each field is either dollars with exactly 2 decimals (from integer cents) or the single character -. The spread field is - unless both a best bid and a best ask exist, in which case it is (best ask cents - best bid cents) printed as dollars with 2 decimals.
constraints: Every cancel C refers to a price level that currently exists on that side and never exceeds the quantity resting there at that moment.
The book never crosses: after every event, best bid <= best ask whenever both sides are non-empty.

examples.explanation: 1) bid 1000, no ask -> 10.00 - -. 2) ask 1005 -> 10.00 10.05 0.05. 3) better ask 1003 -> 10.00 10.03 0.03. 4) the 1005 ask is cancelled away; best ask still 1003. 5) better bid 1002 -> 10.02 10.03 0.01. 6) that bid is cancelled -> back to 10.00 10.03 0.03.
Bid 1000 arrives (no ask). Ask 1002 arrives -> spread 0.02. Bid 1000 cancelled -> bid side empty. Ask 1002 cancelled -> both sides empty. Bid 999 -> 9.99 - -.

hints: One hash map (or dictionary) per side mapping price -> resting quantity is enough. Adds do get(price,0)+qty; cancels do get(price,0)-qty and delete the key when it hits 0.
The best bid is the maximum key of the bid map and the best ask is the minimum key of the ask map. With n <= 3000 events, scanning all keys per event is fast enough.
Keep everything in integer cents and format at print time (cents//100, cents%100 zero-padded). Never convert book prices to floating point.

editorial.text: Approach: two maps and a scan for the extremes

editorial.md: State is just two associative arrays: bids[price] = resting qty, asks[price] = resting qty. Add and cancel are single hash updates, with deletion when a level empties.

editorial.title: Per event
items: Apply the event to the appropriate side map (accumulate on A, subtract on C, erase the key when the quantity reaches 0).
best bid = max key of bids (if any), best ask = min key of asks (if any).
Emit the three fields: missing side -> '-', spread = best ask - best bid in cents only when both exist.

editorial.md: With the stated limits (n <= 3000), scanning the key set of each map per event costs at most O(n * L) where L is the number of live price levels — a few million operations, far under the limit. For much larger inputs you would keep an ordered map per side (best = begin()/rbegin(), O(log L) per event) or a heap with lazy deletion of cancelled levels; both are standard order-book techniques.

A price of c cents is printed as c//100 followed by a dot and c%100 zero-padded to two digits. Doing this in integers avoids any floating-point representation surprise (0.07 is not exactly representable in binary), and the spread is likewise an exact integer subtraction in cents.

editorial.title: Common bugs
editorial.md: 1) Forgetting to delete a level when its quantity reaches 0 (a cancelled level would still be reported as the best price). 2) Printing '-' for the spread even when both sides exist. 3) Treating a cancel at a price with several accumulated adds as removing the whole level — the cancel only removes the stated quantity.
